name: A Mara Conservancy House
flag: Sample entry — replace in the CMS
standfirst: A six-tent house on leased Maasai land bordering the reserve, with its own guides, its own vehicles and no other camp in sight.
opening: Night drives and walking are permitted here in a way they are not inside the national reserve, and the vehicle quota means a sighting is never shared with more than two or three others.

The house sits on a low ridge above a seasonal river, with the tents spaced far enough apart that none is visible from another. Each has a deck facing east, which is the direction the light comes from and the direction the game moves at dawn.
Meals are taken wherever the day has ended up: a long table under the trees, a breakfast laid out at a sighting, dinner by the fire. There is no fixed dining room and no fixed hour.
Members travelling with children are given their own vehicle and a guide used to shorter drives, so the pace of the day belongs to the family rather than to the camp.

openingShots.cap: The conservancy permits night drives, which is most of the reason to stay on one.
The herds pass through between July and October, and the camp moves to meet them.
Balloon mornings are worth one day of a trip, not three.

particulars.label: The rooms
particulars.value: Six tents, two of them family.

particulars.label: Getting in
particulars.value: About 45 minutes by light aircraft from Nairobi Wilson, then a short drive.

particulars.label: Also here
particulars.value: A treatment tent and a plunge pool.

gallery.cap: The crossing season, which peaks in the weeks either side of September.
Walking and night drives are conservancy privileges rather than reserve ones.
Resident game stays on the conservancy year round.
Balloons lift before dawn and land where the wind decides.
Early mornings carry fog across the plain for the first hour.
Six tents on a low ridge, and nothing else within sight of them.

notes.p: Dry season. Grass short, water scarce, animals concentrated, and the river crossings inside this window.
Calving on the short-grass plains to the south, which is quieter and in some ways the better spectacle.
Green, quiet and considerably better value, with superb birdlife and taller grass.
